title: Microbenchmark harness: tokens/sec & p95 regression suite for core models
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create and maintain a lightweight, automated microbenchmark suite focused on tokens/sec and p95 latency for our core inference models. The harness should run synthetic and replay workloads, surface regressions vs baseline, and integrate with our observability/alerting pipeline so regressions generate actionable signals (dashboards + triage tickets). Goals: provide reproducible tokens/sec numbers across model variants and quantization levels, detect >=10% regressions in p95 or tokens/sec, and minimize noise via warmup/KV cache control.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible benchmark runner that measures tokens/sec and p95 for a configurable set of models (open-models and Redwood-verified variants)
Benchmarks can be run locally, CI, and as a scheduled job (K8s CronJob), producing JSON + Prometheus metrics
Regression detection logic: compares current run to baseline (rolling 7-day median) and flags >10% deviation on tokens/sec or p95 with confidence heuristics
Automated alerts: when a regression is detected, a Slack alert and a templated Linear ticket are created with links to the run, diffs, and Grafana snapshots
Bench results include warm vs cold metrics, batching configuration, KV cache state, model binary/quantization tag, and input sequence-length profile
Documentation + runbook covering how to add new models, interpret noise, and triage typical failure modes
implementation_plan: Design runner API: small CLI/python harness that orchestrates tokenized inputs, model invocation, and metric aggregation (support both hosted API and local runtime endpoint)
Synthetic workload: build token generators that follow our production token-length distribution (short/median/long) and include streaming breakpoints
Replay mode: ability to replay sampled production traces (anonymized) to validate tokens/sec under real patterns
Measurement primitives: measure wall-clock token emission rate, per-request p50/p95/p99, and include per-token CPU/GPU utilization hooks where available
Baseline store: push canonical run outputs to an S3 bucket and compute rolling statistics; keep metadata (model sha, quantization tag, runtime flags)
Regression engine: compute percent change vs baseline, apply hysteresis and minimum sample size rules, emit Prometheus 'benchmark_regression' metric with labels
CI integration: add lightweight GitHub Action that runs a smoke microbenchmark for PRs touching runtime kernels or scheduler code; only runs full suite on nightlies or dedicated infra
Alerting/playbook: wire benchmark_regression to Grafana+Alertmanager -> Slack -> Linear (templated body) and include triage checklist
Dashboard: Grafana panel showing tokens/sec and p95 history by model/variant; add heatmap for batch-size vs tokens/sec
Rollout plan: start with 5 core models, iterate to 15 over next 6 weeks; monitor false positives and tune heuristics
tradeoffs_and_notes: Synthetic tests are low-noise and fast but may miss distribution edge cases; replay traces are realistic but require scrubbing and are higher variance
We choose a rolling median baseline to reduce sensitivity to outliers; this increases detection latency for slow degradations but lowers false positives
Running full suites is compute-expensive; prioritize nightly runs and CI smoke checks to balance cost and coverage
Tokens/sec measured at the client boundary (end-to-end) will include network jitter for hosted API — we provide an option to run worker-local measurements to isolate runtime regressions
Quantized model differences: include explicit label for quantization (e.g., int8/q4f16) so regressions are correlated with model artifacts
